g.text: Web app, DB schema, repository layer
Written per course, NOT by us
The instructor owns both yellow boxes
autograder script and the test suite it runs.
The suite is ordinary JUnit or pytest. We do
not generate it, invoke it, or constrain how it
is structured. It imports the reporting library
and calls us with the target names she
The marking logic lives here too. Every
registered target wants feedback by default,
and she opts targets out by calling
ai_not_needed: on passing tests, on a subset,
on any condition she can express in code.
She can also report the outcome via
add_test_result: status for the dashboard, and
run_autograder is hers as well: it decides to
run her suite and then invoke our AI phase.
Thin by design: two calls, an HTTPS client,
and argument validation. One artifact per
It rejects an unregistered target name loudly
on the first call, failing her test run. A
typo that silently succeeds is the worst
failure mode here: everything looks like it
worked and the feedback simply never appears.
A separate command her autograder script
invokes after the test suite exits, never called
from inside her test code. It runs in EVERY
autograder run, including the submission run of
a NIGHTLY assignment, where it asks the service
for one action and performs it: GRADE, DEFER or
It holds no policy. Grading mode, the nightly
authorization flag and the token guard are all
derived server-side, because this code ships
inside the instructor's autograder zip and is
the hardest thing in the system to update.
Log in, then click Rerun Autograder once per
submission that still has an ungraded
submission_target marked ai_needed. It does NOT
call an LLM and does NOT write feedback.
AD-4: the container holds the instructor's
own LLM API key** and calls the providers
directly. Our service never proxies an LLM
call and never sees a provider key.
For an OER this is the right default: each
adopting institution uses its own key and pays
its own bill, so nobody has to run a metered
service or handle someone else's billing.
The container still holds NO database
credential. It reaches our data only through
Two things to settle in the instructor guide,
not in code. How the key gets into the
container, which depends on what secret
facility the platform offers; if the only
route is the uploaded autograder zip, say so
plainly, because a key in a zip is a key in a
backup. And that rotation means touching every
